newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Enami workers to hold brief strike Tues.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Enami workers to hold brief strike Tues.

text.p: Workers at Chile's state copper company Enami will hold a two hour strike Tuesday in protest against the government's reported plans to privatize the firm and state oil producer Enap, said a union leader at Enami.
"The strike will last for two hours as a maximum. It is a warning (to the government)," Luis Guerra, president of the union representing Enami workers, told Reuters.
The walkout will hit Enami's Ventanas and Paipote smelting and refining complexes as well as two small copper processing plants, he said.

President Eduardo Frei will announce plans to sell a controlling stake in two oil refineries, in Concon and Concepcion, owned by Enap in his annual speech to Congress Wednesday, government sources have said.
Local media have said that a special government commission has prepared a study recommending the sale of Enami's plants including Ventanas and Paipote as a way of repaying the company's heavy debts.
Enami buys concentrates from small private mines at prices that allow them to operate economically, leading critics to call it essentially a state subsidy for pits which would otherwise go under.
Union leaders at Enami, Enap and state copper company Codelco have threatened a nationwide strike if the government goes ahead with the plans to sell stakes in Enap and Enami.
The three unions will hold talks Tuesday with Mining Minister Benjamin Teplizky and Frei's top political adviser, Juan Villarzu, but repeated their vow to protest any privatization with walkouts.
"We are sticking to our plans for a national strike, but will be waiting to hear President Frei's speech," said Hernan von Hausen, president of the National Federation of Oil Workers.
